## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

{"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjY5NjM3MjU=","is_bot":false,"login":"yennster","name":"Jenny Speelman"},"baseRefName":"main","body":"The 1 req/sec ThrottleActor set its `nextEarliest` reservation only after
the Task.sleep, so concurrent callers all read the same value, slept to the
same instant, and fired together as a burst. Recent traffic-heavy features
(the live Popular tab's batch of requests, Bookmarks + infinite scroll)
started exercising this hard enough that the app overran AO3's rate limit;
AO3 responds by stalling/tarpitting the client, so requests hang until the
30s URLSession timeout fires — surfacing as "network timeout" errors on
exactly the network-heavy screens (search/browse lists, opening a work).

- ThrottleActor.wait() now reserves each caller's slot atomically *before*
  suspending (actor methods run synchronously up to the first await), so
  concurrent callers get distinct, strictly-spaced instants — never a burst.
- performRequest retries transient failures (URLSession timeouts/dropped
  connections + HTTP 429) with exponential backoff, but only for idempotent
  GETs, so a brief AO3 hiccup recovers instead of failing the whole load
  while POSTs (login/comment/subscribe) never risk a double-submit.
- Add a concurrency regression test asserting N concurrent throttle waits
  are serialized, not bursted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

3	/// Renders one chapter as individual paragraphs, each a scroll anchor
4	/// ("c<chapter>-p<index>") so the reader can restore the exact position.
5	struct ChapterContentView: View {
6	    let chapterIndex: Int
7	    let html: String
8	    let font: Font
9	    let lineSpacing: CGFloat
10	    let paragraphSpacing: CGFloat
11	    let foreground: Color
12	    let scrollSpace: String
13	    /// Letter spacing (kerning) in points, already divided by the UI zoom.
14	    let kerning: CGFloat
15	    /// Render all body text bold.
16	    let boldText: Bool
17	    /// Paragraph index to emphasise while it's being read aloud (TTS karaoke),
18	    /// or nil when this chapter isn't the one narrating.
19	    var highlightParagraph: Int? = nil
20	
21	    @State private var paragraphs: [AttributedString]?
22	
23	    /// Position is sampled every N paragraphs — enough for "resume where you
24	    /// left off" without a GeometryReader on every paragraph (which made
25	    /// scrolling stutter).
26	    private let anchorStride = 6
27	
28	    var body: some View {
29	        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: paragraphSpacing) {
30	            if let paragraphs {
31	                ForEach(Array(paragraphs.enumerated()), id: \.offset) { index, para in
32	                    Text(para)
33	                        .font(font)
34	                        .tracking(kerning)
35	                        .bold(boldText)
36	                        .lineSpacing(lineSpacing)
37	                        .foregroundStyle(foreground)
38	                        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
39	                        // Karaoke highlight: a flush fill behind the paragraph's
40	                        // existing frame, so toggling it never reflows the text.
41	                        .background(
42	                            highlightParagraph == index ? Color.accentColor.opacity(0.15) : Color.clear,
43	                            in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 5)
44	                        )
45	                        .id(ChapterTracking.key(chapter: chapterIndex, paragraph: index))
46	                        .background {
47	                            if index % anchorStride == 0 {
48	                                anchorReporter(paragraph: index)
49	                            }
50	                        }
51	                        .animation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.2), value: highlightParagraph == index)
52	                }
53	            } else {
54	                Text(plainFallback)
55	                    .font(font)
56	                    .tracking(kerning)
57	                    .bold(boldText)
58	                    .lineSpacing(lineSpacing)
59	                    .foregroundStyle(foreground)
60	            }
61	        }
62	        .task(id: html) {
63	            let result = await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) {
64	                HTMLToAttributed.convertParagraphs(html)
65	            }.value
66	            await MainActor.run { paragraphs = result }
67	        }
68	    }
69	
70	    private func anchorReporter(paragraph: Int) -> some View {
71	        GeometryReader { geo in
72	            Color.clear.preference(
73	                key: ScrollAnchorKey.self,
74	                value: [ChapterTracking.key(chapter: chapterIndex, paragraph: paragraph): geo.frame(in: .named(scrollSpace)).minY]
75	            )
76	        }
77	    }
78	
79	    private var plainFallback: String {
80	        html.replacingOccurrences(of: "<[^>]+>", with: "", options: .regularExpression)
81	    }
82	}

content.content:
### SearchPromptParser crashes (NSRangeException) on prompts where lowercasing changes UTF-16 length (e.g. Turkish İ)
parse() builds two parallel buffers: `working` = lowercased prompt and `casedWorking` = original (Fanficly/Search/SearchPromptParser.swift:15-16). extractTitle/extractCreators compute regex match ranges against `working` but call `casedWorking.substring(with:)` with those ranges (lines 51, 71). Characters like U+0130 'İ' lowercase to "i̇" (2 UTF-16 units vs 1), so the buffers desync. Verified crash: prompt "İstanbul by:melis" → working.length 18 vs cased.length 17 → `-[NSString substringWithRange:]: Range {13, 5} out of bounds; string length 17` → uncaught NSInvalidArgumentException, app terminates. Any Turkish-language user typing a fandom/name with İ plus a title:/by:/author: token crashes the app; when the range happens to stay in bounds, the extracted title/creator text is silently shifted by one character per İ (wrong search).
FIX: Don't index one string with ranges computed on another. Match case-insensitively on the ORIGINAL string only (the regexes are already .caseInsensitive or can be) and derive the lowercased comparison per-match, or build `working` via a per-UTF-16-unit lowercase fold that preserves length. Minimal fix: run extractTitle/extractCreators against casedWorking with .caseInsensitive regexes and delete the same range from a working copy kept in lockstep.

### TagResolver permanently caches failed resolutions (offline/429 poisons tag canonicalization for the session)
resolveOne (Fanficly/Search/TagResolver.swift:51-59) unconditionally caches whatever resolveUncached returns. resolveUncached (lines 61-90) swallows every autocomplete error with `try?` and returns the raw typed term when the network fails — including AO3Error.rateLimited and plain offline errors (AO3Client.autocomplete additionally maps any non-JSON body to [] via `try? decode ?? []` at AO3Client.swift:490). Concrete failure: user searches "dramione" or picks a ship filter while briefly offline or 429-throttled → the unresolved literal is cached in the process-lifetime ResolutionCache → for the rest of the session, even with full connectivity, that term is never canonicalized, `work_search[relationship_names]=dramione` matches nothing, and searches silently return zero/wrong results until the app is relaunched.
FIX: Only memoize successful resolutions: have resolveUncached distinguish "autocomplete answered but no match" (cacheable) from "request threw" (do not cache — rethrow or return nil and fall back to the raw term for this one search). Simplest: make resolveUncached return String? where nil means network failure, and skip ResolutionCache.set when nil.

Additionally the count is in a plain `Sherlock Holmes/John Watson (57746)`, not the `span.count` the parser reads. So facets() returns [] for all four kinds on every real page, AO3Client.fetchPopularSnapshot's ship/character aggregation is always empty, and PopularView permanently shows the curated PopularTags fallback — the live-derived Popular ships/characters feature has never worked against production AO3, masked by the fallback and by fixture-only tests. 5 FIX: Change the idPrefix strings passed at MediaCategoryParser.swift:67-70 to `include_work_search_relationship_ids` / `include_work_search_character_ids` / `include_work_search_fandom_ids` / `include_work_search_freeform_ids` (or select `label[for*=__ids]`), and parse the trailing "(N)" from the label's full text via MediaCategoryParser.trailingCount instead of requiring span.count. Add a fixture copied from the live sidebar markup. 6 ==================================================================================================== 7 [major] Deleted reader profiles are instantly resurrected by the iCloud KVS merge 8 FILE: Fanficly/Reader/ReaderProfileSyncStore.swift 9 DETAIL: ReaderView.deleteProfile (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift:128-141) removes the profile from the list and calls saveProfiles -> ReaderProfileSyncStore.publishLocalProfiles (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderProfileSyncStore.swift:25-38). publishLocalProfiles merges the new local list INTO the cloud copy via ReaderProfile.mergedProfiles (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderProfile.swift:141-153), which is a pure union: it starts from the cloud list (which still contains the deleted profile, since every prior save published the full list to NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore) and only overwrites/appends incoming names — it never removes anything. The merged JSON (deleted profile included) is then written straight back to UserDefaults "reader.profiles" (line 31-33), which the @AppStorage-backed profiles list observes. Failure scenario: user opens the Aa menu, deletes profile "Night", and it reappears in the menu immediately (or, at latest, on the next didChangeExternallyNotification via syncCloudToLocal, lines 40-59). Deletion never sticks on any device once the profile has been published to KVS — and NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore caches locally, so this happens even without an active iCloud account. 10 FIX: Make deletions first-class in the merge: keep a per-profile updatedAt (or a tombstone list of deleted names with timestamps) in the synced JSON, and have mergedProfiles drop profiles whose tombstone is newer than their profile entry. Minimal stopgap: in publishLocalProfiles, treat the incoming local list as authoritative for names it used to contain (publish the local list as-is instead of unioning with cloud) and only union in syncCloudToLocal. 11 ==================================================================================================== 12 [major] Reading-time stats accrue while the reader is covered by a pushed view (phantom/double-counted time) 13 FILE: Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift 14 DETAIL: ReaderLifecycleModifier (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift:267-291) starts the active-reading timer on every scenePhase transition to .active, with no check that the reader is actually visible. A ReaderView covered by a pushed view (e.g. tapping the byline -> AuthorWorksView, or opening another work -> a second ReaderView) stays installed in the NavigationStack, so its onChange(of: scenePhase) still fires. Failure scenario: (1) open work A's reader; (2) tap "by author" — reader A gets onDisappear, timer correctly flushed to nil; (3) background the app and return — reader A's scenePhase handler calls startReadingTimer() (line 670-672), setting activeSpanStart while A is not on screen; (4) browse the author's works for 30 minutes, then background again — flushTimer -> recordReadingSpan (line 678-704) records ~30 minutes of reading time against work A that never happened. If the user opened work B's reader in the meantime, both readers record the same wall-clock span, double-counting totals in the Stats tab. Repeats on every background/foreground cycle while covered, up to the 4h cap each time. 15 FIX: Track visibility with a @State isVisible flag set true in onAppear and false in onDisappear, and guard startTimer: on scenePhase .active only call startReadingTimer() when isVisible (flushTimer on leaving .active is already safe to run unconditionally). 16 ==================================================================================================== 17 [major] Progress can never reach the Finished threshold for typical works in continuous mode — 'stories read' undercounts 18 FILE: Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift 19 DETAIL: In continuous mode the saved paragraph anchor is quantized twice: ChapterContentView only emits a scroll anchor every 6th paragraph (anchorStride, Fanficly/Reader/ChapterContentView.swift:36,67-71), and ChapterTracking.topmostAnchor (Fanficly/Reader/ChapterTracking.swift:42-48) picks the anchor at/above y=80 — i.e. the paragraph near the TOP of the viewport, roughly one screenful before the end. readingProgressFraction (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift:730-743) computes paragraph/(count-1) from that anchor, so scrolling a chapter fully to the bottom yields max progress of about (count − paragraphsPerScreen, rounded down to a multiple of 6)/(count−1). Failure scenario: a complete single-chapter one-shot with 60 paragraphs and ~12 on the final screen tops out around anchor 48 -> 48/59 ≈ 0.81. That is below both Finished thresholds (>=0.99, or >=0.95 for complete works — ReadingStatSnapshot.isFinished, Fanficly/Reader/ReadingProgressStore.swift:90-92, and the Library badge in LibraryView.swift:432-434). The user reads the whole fic to the last line, the Library row shows "81% read" forever, the work never gets the Finished badge, never counts in Stats "stories read", and words-read is permanently ~20% short. Continuous is the default reading mode, and one-shots are the common case, so this hits most users. Page-by-page has a milder version (anchor = first paragraph of the current page, ReaderView.swift:1132-1138). 20 FIX: Detect end-of-content explicitly: when the scroll view reaches (or the last page shows) the final paragraph of the final chapter, save the anchor as the last paragraph index (progress 1.0) — e.g. add an anchor reporter on the last paragraph regardless of stride, and in topmostAnchor/save logic treat 'bottom of content visible' as the last anchor. Alternatively compute progress from scroll offset within the chapter rather than the topmost-visible anchor. 21 ==================================================================================================== 22 [blocker] iCloud backup is whole-file last-writer-wins: a second device with a smaller library silently shrinks the backup, losing works on restore 23 FILE: Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift 24 DETAIL: backupToiCloud (Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift:63-249) serializes only the local device's records and overwrites the single library_backup.json (atomic write at line 245). queueBackup is auto-invoked from every mutation (star/pin/follow/folder edits throughout LibraryView.swift, WorkPersistence.swift:110/172/181), so whichever device touched anything last defines the entire cloud backup. Meanwhile the launch restore (FanficlyApp.swift:122-128) only runs when worksCount == 0, so a non-empty device never pulls the other device's works before overwriting. Concrete scenario: iPhone has 50 saved works, iPad has 5, both have settings.iCloudSyncEnabled on. User stars one work on the iPad -> 2s later the iPad writes a 5-work backup over the 50-work one. iPhone is lost/replaced; the new iPhone restores from iCloud and gets 5 works — 45 works (and their reading state) are gone, with no error anywhere. 25 FIX: Merge before writing: in backupToiCloud, first decode the existing cloud file and union it with local state (same per-record merge rules restoreFromiCloud uses) before encoding, or refuse to overwrite a backup whose timestamp is newer than the last local restore. Alternatively run restoreFromiCloud (which merges additively) before every backup write. 26 ==================================================================================================== 27 [major] Restore deletes locally downloaded chapters when the backup's copy of the work has no/fewer chapters 28 FILE: Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift 29 DETAIL: restoreFromiCloud (Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift:440-448) unconditionally does `for ch in work.chapters { context.delete(ch) }` / `work.chapters.removeAll()` and then inserts only the backup's chapters. A work that was merely followed (metadata upsert via WorkPersistence.upsertMetadata, no chapter bodies) backs up with `chapters: []`. Concrete scenario: user downloads a 40-chapter fic for offline reading on the iPhone; on the iPad they follow the same fic (metadata only); the iPad's backup wins the last-writer-wins race (see blocker above); user later taps Restore in Settings on the iPhone (SettingsView.swift:58/87/119 — reachable even with a full library, unlike the launch path). The iPhone's 40 downloaded chapter bodies are deleted and replaced with zero chapters — offline content silently destroyed while the row still shows the green Downloaded badge (badge keys off the epub file, LibraryView.swift:53/155). 30 FIX: Only replace chapters when the backup actually has them and they differ: `if !w.chapters.isEmpty { ...delete+insert... }` (optionally also skip when local count >= backup count). While there, carry Chapter.aoId through ChapterBackup (see separate finding). 31 ==================================================================================================== 32 [major] ReadingStat merge breaks totalSeconds == sum(daySeconds): All Time can show less reading time than a single Year/Month period after a cross-device restore 33 FILE: Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift 34 DETAIL: In restoreFromiCloud (Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift:549-558), the merge sets `existing.totalSeconds = max(existing.totalSeconds, st.totalSeconds)` but unions daySeconds with per-day maxima. Those two rules disagree whenever the devices read the same work on different days. Concrete scenario: iPhone reads work X for 1000s on Monday (totalSeconds=1000, {Mon:1000}); iPad reads X for 2000s on Tuesday (totalSeconds=2000, {Tue:2000}); after restore the row has daySeconds {Mon:1000, Tue:2000} (sum 3000) but totalSeconds = max(1000,2000) = 2000. ReadingStatsAggregator.summarize (Fanficly/Reader/ReadingProgressStore.swift:182-190) uses totalSeconds for All Time but sums daySeconds for a period, so the Stats tab shows Year 2026 = 50m while All Time = 33m — visibly impossible. Related undercount in the same merge: two devices reading the same work on the same day keep only max(dayA, dayB), not the sum, so half the reading time is dropped (documented as 'conservative', but combined with the max-total rule the numbers are internally inconsistent, not just conservative). 35 FIX: After merging daySeconds, recompute the total from the merged buckets: `existing.totalSeconds = max(existing.totalSeconds, merged.values.reduce(0, +))` (the max keeps pre-daySeconds legacy totals from shrinking). That restores the totalSeconds >= sum(period) invariant the aggregator assumes. 36 ==================================================================================================== 37 [major] Stale AO3 session wipes every SubscriptionRecord (and its notification baselines) on the next sync 38 FILE: Fanficly/Subscriptions/SubscriptionPoller.swift 39 DETAIL: SubscriptionPoller.syncSubscriptionList (Fanficly/Subscriptions/SubscriptionPoller.swift:38-40) deletes every SubscriptionRecord whose key is not in the freshly fetched list. When the AO3 session cookie has expired (or Keychain cookies were unreadable at BG launch), GET /users//subscriptions 302-redirects to the login page; URLSession follows the redirect so AO3Client.performRequest (Fanficly/Networking/AO3Client.swift:574-586) sees a 200 and returns the login-page HTML. Result: the 4-hourly background poll (runFullPoll → syncSubscriptionList) deletes ALL real subscription records, including their lastSeenChapterCount baselines, and inserts junk rows. Concrete scenario: user's remember-me cookie expires after ~2 weeks; that night's background poll silently deletes their 40 subscriptions; they re-log-in, the next sync recreates records with lastSeenChapterCount = nil, and the first check just re-baselines — every chapter posted in the interim is never notified, and the Subscriptions tab briefly shows bogus 'login' rows. 40 FIX: Make the sync fail closed: have SubscriptionsParser throw AO3Error.parseFailed (or AO3Client throw .unauthorized) when the page has no subscription index markers (e.g. missing dl.subscription / the logged-in nav), and in syncSubscriptionList skip the delete pass when `fresh` is empty or the parse looks like a non-subscriptions page. 41 ==================================================================================================== 42 [major] Notification permission is never requested for the local-follow flow, so follow/author alerts are silently dropped 43 FILE: Fanficly/Subscriptions/SubscriptionsView.swift 44 DETAIL: The only call to NotificationsAuthorization.request() is in SubscriptionsView's .task and it is gated on auth.username != nil (Fanficly/Subscriptions/SubscriptionsView.swift:123-128). WorkPersistence.toggleFollow / toggleFollowAuthor never request authorization, and neither does the app at launch. Per the project docs, local follows are the headline logged-out feature ('fires a local notification — works fully logged out'). Concrete scenario: a logged-out user follows 5 works via the bookmark button; authorizationStatus stays .notDetermined forever (the Subscriptions tab only shows a login gate for them); every UNUserNotificationCenter.add in postNewChapterNotification / postNewWorkNotification throws 'notifications not allowed' and is swallowed by try? (SubscriptionPoller.swift:168, 185). The user never receives a single new-chapter alert. Even logged-in users get nothing until they happen to open the Subscriptions tab once. 45 FIX: Call NotificationsAuthorization.request() at the point a user first follows a work or author (WorkPersistence.toggleFollow / toggleFollowAuthor call sites, or a .task in FollowedAuthorsView/LibraryView), independent of login state. 46 ==================================================================================================== 47 [major] fetchSubscriptions only reads page 1, so users with >20 AO3 subscriptions permanently lose the rest 48 FILE: Fanficly/Networking/AO3Client.swift 49 DETAIL: AO3Endpoints.userSubscriptions has no page parameter (Fanficly/Networking/AO3Endpoints.swift:47-49) and AO3Client.fetchSubscriptions (AO3Client.swift:354-362) fetches a single page; AO3 paginates the subscriptions index at 20 per page. Because syncSubscriptionList deletes any record not present in the fetched list (SubscriptionPoller.swift:38-40), subscriptions on page 2+ are never inserted — and if AO3's ordering shifts a work across the page boundary, its record (with its lastSeenChapterCount baseline) is deleted and later recreated with a nil baseline. Concrete scenario: a user with 35 AO3 subscriptions sees only 20 in the Subscriptions tab and never gets new-chapter notifications for the other 15; works oscillating across the page-1 boundary repeatedly lose their baseline so their updates are also missed. 50 FIX: Loop pages in fetchSubscriptions (add page param to AO3Endpoints.userSubscriptions and follow AO3's pagination until the last page), or at minimum stop deleting records that weren't returned when the fetch was single-page/truncated. 51 ==================================================================================================== 52 [major] Fixed poll order + 1 req/s throttle starves author follows (and late followed works) inside the ~30 s BG refresh budget 53 FILE: Fanficly/Subscriptions/SubscriptionPoller.swift 54 DETAIL: checkFollowedWorks and checkFollowedAuthors run ONLY from the background task (grep confirms runFullPoll's sole caller is BackgroundRefresh.runPoll; SubscriptionsView.refresh runs just the sub sync + checkForNewChapters). runFullPoll (SubscriptionPoller.swift:136-150) issues one throttled request (1 req/s, ThrottleActor) per subscription, then per followed work, then per followed author — always in that order. A BGAppRefreshTask gets roughly 30 seconds, so only ~25 requests ever complete before SwiftUI cancels the task; every fetch after cancellation throws immediately and is logged as 'Skipping…'. Concrete scenario: a user with 20 AO3 subscriptions and 15 followed works follows an author; every background poll spends its whole budget on the same head-of-list subscriptions/works, checkFollowedAuthors never gets a successful fetch, and author-follow notifications simply never fire — with no error surfaced anywhere. 55 FIX: Persist a per-record lastCheckedAt cursor and poll oldest-checked-first across all three categories (round-robin), so every record eventually gets its turn across successive BG windows; optionally also schedule a BGProcessingTask for larger libraries. 56 ==================================================================================================== 57 [major] Tapping a stale widget regresses the saved reading position 58 FILE: Fanficly/RootView.swift 59 DETAIL: RootView.installResumeProgressIfAvailable (Fanficly/RootView.swift:277-304) prefers the anchor baked into the tapped widget URL over everything else (`route.anchor ?? widgetAnchor`, line 292). (2) If the user has since read a different work, WidgetProgressStore.load() returns that other work, matchingWidgetProgress is nil, and the freshness guard is skipped entirely. Concrete scenario: read work A to chapter 10 tonight; the widget still shows this morning's snapshot at chapter 2; tapping it rewrites ReadingProgress to chapter 2/paragraph N (ReadingProgressStore.save overwrites unconditionally) and the reader restores there — the chapter-10 position is lost. 60 FIX: Never let a URL anchor move progress backwards: only apply route.anchor when it is fresher than the existing ReadingProgress (compare against existing.updatedAt with >=, and prefer the widget-store anchor over the URL anchor when the store entry for that work is newer); otherwise just navigate and let the saved progress win. 61

file.content: ==================================================================================================== [major] WorkFiltersParser facet selectors don't match live AO3 markup — Popular ships/characters silently never live FILE: Fanficly/Networking/HTMLParsers/MediaCategoryParser.swift DETAIL: WorkFiltersParser.facets (Fanficly/Networking/HTMLParsers/MediaCategoryParser.swift:77-91) selects `label[for^=include_relationship_ids]` etc., but live AO3 works pages use `for="include_work_search_relationship_ids_"` — verified by fetching https://archiveofourown.org/tags/Sherlock%20(BBC%20TV%202010)/works: zero labels match `include_relationship_ids*`, all match `include_work_search_relationship_ids*`. Additionally the count is in a plain `Sherlock Holmes/John Watson (57746)`, not the `span.count` the parser reads. So facets() returns [] for all four kinds on every real page, AO3Client.fetchPopularSnapshot's ship/character aggregation is always empty, and PopularView permanently shows the curated PopularTags fallback — the live-derived Popular ships/characters feature has never worked against production AO3, masked by the fallback and by fixture-only tests. FIX: Change the idPrefix strings passed at MediaCategoryParser.swift:67-70 to `include_work_search_relationship_ids` / `include_work_search_character_ids` / `include_work_search_fandom_ids` / `include_work_search_freeform_ids` (or select `label[for*=__ids]`), and parse the trailing "(N)" from the label's full text via MediaCategoryParser.trailingCount instead of requiring span.count. Add a fixture copied from the live sidebar markup. ==================================================================================================== [major] Deleted reader profiles are instantly resurrected by the iCloud KVS merge FILE: Fanficly/Reader/ReaderProfileSyncStore.swift DETAIL: ReaderView.deleteProfile (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift:128-141) removes the profile from the list and calls saveProfiles -> ReaderProfileSyncStore.publishLocalProfiles (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderProfileSyncStore.swift:25-38). publishLocalProfiles merges the new local list INTO the cloud copy via ReaderProfile.mergedProfiles (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderProfile.swift:141-153), which is a pure union: it starts from the cloud list (which still contains the deleted profile, since every prior save published the full list to NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore) and only overwrites/appends incoming names — it never removes anything. The merged JSON (deleted profile included) is then written straight back to UserDefaults "reader.profiles" (line 31-33), which the @AppStorage-backed profiles list observes. Failure scenario: user opens the Aa menu, deletes profile "Night", and it reappears in the menu immediately (or, at latest, on the next didChangeExternallyNotification via syncCloudToLocal, lines 40-59). Deletion never sticks on any device once the profile has been published to KVS — and NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore caches locally, so this happens even without an active iCloud account. FIX: Make deletions first-class in the merge: keep a per-profile updatedAt (or a tombstone list of deleted names with timestamps) in the synced JSON, and have mergedProfiles drop profiles whose tombstone is newer than their profile entry. Minimal stopgap: in publishLocalProfiles, treat the incoming local list as authoritative for names it used to contain (publish the local list as-is instead of unioning with cloud) and only union in syncCloudToLocal. ==================================================================================================== [major] Reading-time stats accrue while the reader is covered by a pushed view (phantom/double-counted time) FILE: Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift DETAIL: ReaderLifecycleModifier (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift:267-291) starts the active-reading timer on every scenePhase transition to .active, with no check that the reader is actually visible. A ReaderView covered by a pushed view (e.g. tapping the byline -> AuthorWorksView, or opening another work -> a second ReaderView) stays installed in the NavigationStack, so its onChange(of: scenePhase) still fires. Failure scenario: (1) open work A's reader; (2) tap "by author" — reader A gets onDisappear, timer correctly flushed to nil; (3) background the app and return — reader A's scenePhase handler calls startReadingTimer() (line 670-672), setting activeSpanStart while A is not on screen; (4) browse the author's works for 30 minutes, then background again — flushTimer -> recordReadingSpan (line 678-704) records ~30 minutes of reading time against work A that never happened. If the user opened work B's reader in the meantime, both readers record the same wall-clock span, double-counting totals in the Stats tab. Repeats on every background/foreground cycle while covered, up to the 4h cap each time. FIX: Track visibility with a @State isVisible flag set true in onAppear and false in onDisappear, and guard startTimer: on scenePhase .active only call startReadingTimer() when isVisible (flushTimer on leaving .active is already safe to run unconditionally). ==================================================================================================== [major] Progress can never reach the Finished threshold for typical works in continuous mode — 'stories read' undercounts FILE: Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift DETAIL: In continuous mode the saved paragraph anchor is quantized twice: ChapterContentView only emits a scroll anchor every 6th paragraph (anchorStride, Fanficly/Reader/ChapterContentView.swift:36,67-71), and ChapterTracking.topmostAnchor (Fanficly/Reader/ChapterTracking.swift:42-48) picks the anchor at/above y=80 — i.e. the paragraph near the TOP of the viewport, roughly one screenful before the end. readingProgressFraction (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift:730-743) computes paragraph/(count-1) from that anchor, so scrolling a chapter fully to the bottom yields max progress of about (count − paragraphsPerScreen, rounded down to a multiple of 6)/(count−1). Failure scenario: a complete single-chapter one-shot with 60 paragraphs and ~12 on the final screen tops out around anchor 48 -> 48/59 ≈ 0.81. That is below both Finished thresholds (>=0.99, or >=0.95 for complete works — ReadingStatSnapshot.isFinished, Fanficly/Reader/ReadingProgressStore.swift:90-92, and the Library badge in LibraryView.swift:432-434). The user reads the whole fic to the last line, the Library row shows "81% read" forever, the work never gets the Finished badge, never counts in Stats "stories read", and words-read is permanently ~20% short. Continuous is the default reading mode, and one-shots are the common case, so this hits most users. Page-by-page has a milder version (anchor = first paragraph of the current page, ReaderView.swift:1132-1138). FIX: Detect end-of-content explicitly: when the scroll view reaches (or the last page shows) the final paragraph of the final chapter, save the anchor as the last paragraph index (progress 1.0) — e.g. add an anchor reporter on the last paragraph regardless of stride, and in topmostAnchor/save logic treat 'bottom of content visible' as the last anchor. Alternatively compute progress from scroll offset within the chapter rather than the topmost-visible anchor. ==================================================================================================== [blocker] iCloud backup is whole-file last-writer-wins: a second device with a smaller library silently shrinks the backup, losing works on restore FILE: Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift DETAIL: backupToiCloud (Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift:63-249) serializes only the local device's records and overwrites the single library_backup.json (atomic write at line 245). queueBackup is auto-invoked from every mutation (star/pin/follow/folder edits throughout LibraryView.swift, WorkPersistence.swift:110/172/181), so whichever device touched anything last defines the entire cloud backup. Meanwhile the launch restore (FanficlyApp.swift:122-128) only runs when worksCount == 0, so a non-empty device never pulls the other device's works before overwriting. Concrete scenario: iPhone has 50 saved works, iPad has 5, both have settings.iCloudSyncEnabled on. User stars one work on the iPad -> 2s later the iPad writes a 5-work backup over the 50-work one. iPhone is lost/replaced; the new iPhone restores from iCloud and gets 5 works — 45 works (and their reading state) are gone, with no error anywhere. FIX: Merge before writing: in backupToiCloud, first decode the existing cloud file and union it with local state (same per-record merge rules restoreFromiCloud uses) before encoding, or refuse to overwrite a backup whose timestamp is newer than the last local restore. Alternatively run restoreFromiCloud (which merges additively) before every backup write. ==================================================================================================== [major] Restore deletes locally downloaded chapters when the backup's copy of the work has no/fewer chapters FILE: Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift DETAIL: restoreFromiCloud (Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift:440-448) unconditionally does `for ch in work.chapters { context.delete(ch) }` / `work.chapters.removeAll()` and then inserts only the backup's chapters. A work that was merely followed (metadata upsert via WorkPersistence.upsertMetadata, no chapter bodies) backs up with `chapters: []`. Concrete scenario: user downloads a 40-chapter fic for offline reading on the iPhone; on the iPad they follow the same fic (metadata only); the iPad's backup wins the last-writer-wins race (see blocker above); user later taps Restore in Settings on the iPhone (SettingsView.swift:58/87/119 — reachable even with a full library, unlike the launch path). The iPhone's 40 downloaded chapter bodies are deleted and replaced with zero chapters — offline content silently destroyed while the row still shows the green Downloaded badge (badge keys off the epub file, LibraryView.swift:53/155). FIX: Only replace chapters when the backup actually has them and they differ: `if !w.chapters.isEmpty { ...delete+insert... }` (optionally also skip when local count >= backup count). While there, carry Chapter.aoId through ChapterBackup (see separate finding). ==================================================================================================== [major] ReadingStat merge breaks totalSeconds == sum(daySeconds): All Time can show less reading time than a single Year/Month period after a cross-device restore FILE: Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift DETAIL: In restoreFromiCloud (Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift:549-558), the merge sets `existing.totalSeconds = max(existing.totalSeconds, st.totalSeconds)` but unions daySeconds with per-day maxima. Those two rules disagree whenever the devices read the same work on different days. Concrete scenario: iPhone reads work X for 1000s on Monday (totalSeconds=1000, {Mon:1000}); iPad reads X for 2000s on Tuesday (totalSeconds=2000, {Tue:2000}); after restore the row has daySeconds {Mon:1000, Tue:2000} (sum 3000) but totalSeconds = max(1000,2000) = 2000. ReadingStatsAggregator.summarize (Fanficly/Reader/ReadingProgressStore.swift:182-190) uses totalSeconds for All Time but sums daySeconds for a period, so the Stats tab shows Year 2026 = 50m while All Time = 33m — visibly impossible. Related undercount in the same merge: two devices reading the same work on the same day keep only max(dayA, dayB), not the sum, so half the reading time is dropped (documented as 'conservative', but combined with the max-total rule the numbers are internally inconsistent, not just conservative). FIX: After merging daySeconds, recompute the total from the merged buckets: `existing.totalSeconds = max(existing.totalSeconds, merged.values.reduce(0, +))` (the max keeps pre-daySeconds legacy totals from shrinking). That restores the totalSeconds >= sum(period) invariant the aggregator assumes. ==================================================================================================== [major] Stale AO3 session wipes every SubscriptionRecord (and its notification baselines) on the next sync FILE: Fanficly/Subscriptions/SubscriptionPoller.swift DETAIL: SubscriptionPoller.syncSubscriptionList (Fanficly/Subscriptions/SubscriptionPoller.swift:38-40) deletes every SubscriptionRecord whose key is not in the freshly fetched list. When the AO3 session cookie has expired (or Keychain cookies were unreadable at BG launch), GET /users//subscriptions 302-redirects to the login page; URLSession follows the redirect so AO3Client.performRequest (Fanficly/Networking/AO3Client.swift:574-586) sees a 200 and returns the login-page HTML. SubscriptionsParser.parse never throws for a wrong page — with no subscription containers it scans the whole doc (SubscriptionsParser.swift:24-27) and classify() even turns the login page's '/users/login' link into a phantom 'user:login' subscription (SubscriptionsParser.swift:90-94). Result: the 4-hourly background poll (runFullPoll → syncSubscriptionList) deletes ALL real subscription records, including their lastSeenChapterCount baselines, and inserts junk rows. Concrete scenario: user's remember-me cookie expires after ~2 weeks; that night's background poll silently deletes their 40 subscriptions; they re-log-in, the next sync recreates records with lastSeenChapterCount = nil, and the first check just re-baselines — every chapter posted in the interim is never notified, and the Subscriptions tab briefly shows bogus 'login' rows. FIX: Make the sync fail closed: have SubscriptionsParser throw AO3Error.parseFailed (or AO3Client throw .unauthorized) when the page has no subscription index markers (e.g. missing dl.subscription / the logged-in nav), and in syncSubscriptionList skip the delete pass when `fresh` is empty or the parse looks like a non-subscriptions page. ==================================================================================================== [major] Notification permission is never requested for the local-follow flow, so follow/author alerts are silently dropped FILE: Fanficly/Subscriptions/SubscriptionsView.swift DETAIL: The only call to NotificationsAuthorization.request() is in SubscriptionsView's .task and it is gated on auth.username != nil (Fanficly/Subscriptions/SubscriptionsView.swift:123-128). WorkPersistence.toggleFollow / toggleFollowAuthor never request authorization, and neither does the app at launch. Per the project docs, local follows are the headline logged-out feature ('fires a local notification — works fully logged out'). Concrete scenario: a logged-out user follows 5 works via the bookmark button; authorizationStatus stays .notDetermined forever (the Subscriptions tab only shows a login gate for them); every UNUserNotificationCenter.add in postNewChapterNotification / postNewWorkNotification throws 'notifications not allowed' and is swallowed by try? (SubscriptionPoller.swift:168, 185). The user never receives a single new-chapter alert. Even logged-in users get nothing until they happen to open the Subscriptions tab once. FIX: Call NotificationsAuthorization.request() at the point a user first follows a work or author (WorkPersistence.toggleFollow / toggleFollowAuthor call sites, or a .task in FollowedAuthorsView/LibraryView), independent of login state. ==================================================================================================== [major] fetchSubscriptions only reads page 1, so users with >20 AO3 subscriptions permanently lose the rest FILE: Fanficly/Networking/AO3Client.swift DETAIL: AO3Endpoints.userSubscriptions has no page parameter (Fanficly/Networking/AO3Endpoints.swift:47-49) and AO3Client.fetchSubscriptions (AO3Client.swift:354-362) fetches a single page; AO3 paginates the subscriptions index at 20 per page. Because syncSubscriptionList deletes any record not present in the fetched list (SubscriptionPoller.swift:38-40), subscriptions on page 2+ are never inserted — and if AO3's ordering shifts a work across the page boundary, its record (with its lastSeenChapterCount baseline) is deleted and later recreated with a nil baseline. Concrete scenario: a user with 35 AO3 subscriptions sees only 20 in the Subscriptions tab and never gets new-chapter notifications for the other 15; works oscillating across the page-1 boundary repeatedly lose their baseline so their updates are also missed. FIX: Loop pages in fetchSubscriptions (add page param to AO3Endpoints.userSubscriptions and follow AO3's pagination until the last page), or at minimum stop deleting records that weren't returned when the fetch was single-page/truncated. ==================================================================================================== [major] Fixed poll order + 1 req/s throttle starves author follows (and late followed works) inside the ~30 s BG refresh budget FILE: Fanficly/Subscriptions/SubscriptionPoller.swift DETAIL: checkFollowedWorks and checkFollowedAuthors run ONLY from the background task (grep confirms runFullPoll's sole caller is BackgroundRefresh.runPoll; SubscriptionsView.refresh runs just the sub sync + checkForNewChapters). runFullPoll (SubscriptionPoller.swift:136-150) issues one throttled request (1 req/s, ThrottleActor) per subscription, then per followed work, then per followed author — always in that order. A BGAppRefreshTask gets roughly 30 seconds, so only ~25 requests ever complete before SwiftUI cancels the task; every fetch after cancellation throws immediately and is logged as 'Skipping…'. Concrete scenario: a user with 20 AO3 subscriptions and 15 followed works follows an author; every background poll spends its whole budget on the same head-of-list subscriptions/works, checkFollowedAuthors never gets a successful fetch, and author-follow notifications simply never fire — with no error surfaced anywhere. FIX: Persist a per-record lastCheckedAt cursor and poll oldest-checked-first across all three categories (round-robin), so every record eventually gets its turn across successive BG windows; optionally also schedule a BGProcessingTask for larger libraries. ==================================================================================================== [major] Tapping a stale widget regresses the saved reading position FILE: Fanficly/RootView.swift DETAIL: RootView.installResumeProgressIfAvailable (Fanficly/RootView.swift:277-304) prefers the anchor baked into the tapped widget URL over everything else (`route.anchor ?? widgetAnchor`, line 292). Two failure paths: (1) ReadingProgressStore.save stamps ReadingProgress.updatedAt and the WidgetProgressStore payload with the SAME `now` (ReadingProgressStore.swift:15-54), so the freshness guard `existing.updatedAt > matchingWidgetProgress.freshnessDate` (RootView.swift:281-284) is strict-greater and never trips for the current work — the code then unconditionally writes the URL's chapter/paragraph into ReadingProgress. WidgetKit timeline reloads are budget-throttled, so the home-screen widget (and its deep-link URL, FanficlyWidget.swift:120-136) can lag hours behind. (2) If the user has since read a different work, WidgetProgressStore.load() returns that other work, matchingWidgetProgress is nil, and the freshness guard is skipped entirely. Concrete scenario: read work A to chapter 10 tonight; the widget still shows this morning's snapshot at chapter 2; tapping it rewrites ReadingProgress to chapter 2/paragraph N (ReadingProgressStore.save overwrites unconditionally) and the reader restores there — the chapter-10 position is lost. FIX: Never let a URL anchor move progress backwards: only apply route.anchor when it is fresher than the existing ReadingProgress (compare against existing.updatedAt with >=, and prefer the widget-store anchor over the URL anchor when the store entry for that work is newer); otherwise just navigate and let the saved progress win.

input.prompt:
Fix three confirmed data-loss bugs in Fanficly/Library/iCloudSyncManager.swift (repo /Users/jenny/Work/ao3-app), found by an adversarially-verified multi-agent audit:

1. BLOCKER — whole-file last-writer-wins backup: backupToiCloud (~lines 63-249) serializes only the local device's records and atomically overwrites library_backup.json. queueBackup fires on every mutation (LibraryView.swift, WorkPersistence.swift:110/172/181), and the launch restore (FanficlyApp.swift:122-128) only runs when worksCount == 0. Scenario: iPhone has 50 works, iPad has 5; iPad stars one work → 5-work backup overwrites the 50-work one; a replacement iPhone restores 5 works, 45 silently lost. 2. MAJOR — restore deletes downloaded chapters: restoreFromiCloud (~lines 440-448) unconditionally deletes work.chapters and inserts the backup's chapters. A metadata-only follow backs up with chapters: [], so restoring wipes a 40-chapter offline download while the green Downloaded badge stays (badge keys off the epub file). Also carry Chapter.aoId through ChapterBackup — restore currently drops it, degrading per-chapter comments.

3. MAJOR — ReadingStat merge breaks totalSeconds == sum(daySeconds): restore merge (~lines 549-558) takes max of totalSeconds but unions daySeconds per-day maxima, so All Time can show LESS than a single Year period (iPhone 1000s Monday + iPad 2000s Tuesday → daySeconds sums 3000 but totalSeconds = 2000). Fix: after merging daySeconds, set existing.totalSeconds = max(existing.totalSeconds, mergedDaySeconds.values.reduce(0,+)).

input.title: Fix subscription sync & notification reliability
input.prompt:
Fix four confirmed reliability bugs in Fanficly's subscriptions/notifications (repo /Users/jenny/Work/ao3-app), found by an adversarially-verified multi-agent audit:

1. Stale AO3 session wipes all SubscriptionRecords: SubscriptionPoller.syncSubscriptionList (Fanficly/Subscriptions/SubscriptionPoller.swift:38-40) deletes records absent from a fresh fetch. With an expired cookie, /users/<name>/subscriptions 302s to the login page, URLSession follows it, performRequest sees 200, and SubscriptionsParser scans the login page without throwing (SubscriptionsParser.swift:24-27; classify() even makes a phantom 'user:login' row from the /users/login link at lines 90-94). Nightly BG poll then deletes all real records + their lastSeenChapterCount baselines. Fix: fail closed — have the parser throw when the page lacks subscription-index markers, and skip the delete pass when the fetch is empty/suspect.

2. fetchSubscriptions reads only page 1 (20 subs): AO3Endpoints.userSubscriptions has no page param (AO3Endpoints.swift:47-49); AO3Client.fetchSubscriptions (AO3Client.swift:354-362) fetches once. Users with >20 subs lose the rest, and boundary-crossing works repeatedly lose baselines. Fix: paginate until the last page (respect the 1 req/s throttle).

3. Notification permission never requested for local follows: the only NotificationsAuthorization.request() call is gated on auth.username != nil (SubscriptionsView.swift:123-128), but local follows are the headline logged-out feature; UNUserNotificationCenter.add failures are swallowed by try? (SubscriptionPoller.swift:168/185), so logged-out followers never get any alert. Fix: request authorization when the user first follows a work/author (WorkPersistence.toggleFollow / toggleFollowAuthor call sites or a .task in the relevant views), independent of login.

4. Fixed poll order starves author follows: runFullPoll (SubscriptionPoller.swift:136-150) polls subs → followed works → followed authors, one throttled req/sec each, but a BGAppRefreshTask gets ~30s, so with ~25+ records the author checks never run. Fix: persist per-record lastCheckedAt and poll oldest-first round-robin across all three categories so every record eventually gets a turn.

Add parser tests (login-page fixture must throw / not produce phantom subs) and endpoint pagination tests. Run: DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer xcodebuild test -project Fanficly.xcodeproj -scheme Fanficly -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO -only-testing:FanficlyTests

input.title: Fix reading-stats accuracy (phantom time, Finished threshold)
input.prompt:
Fix two confirmed stats-accuracy bugs in the Fanficly reader (repo /Users/jenny/Work/ao3-app), found by an adversarially-verified multi-agent audit:

1. Reading time accrues while the reader is covered: ReaderLifecycleModifier (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift:267-291) restarts the active-reading timer on every scenePhase → .active with no visibility check. A ReaderView left in the NavigationStack under a pushed view (author page, second reader) restarts its timer on foregrounding (startReadingTimer call ~line 670-672) and records phantom time — two stacked readers double-count the same wall-clock span into ReadingStat, up to the 4h cap per cycle. Fix: track an isVisible @State (true in onAppear, false in onDisappear) and only startReadingTimer() on .active when visible; flushing on inactive stays unconditional.

2. Progress can't reach the Finished threshold in continuous mode: anchors are sampled every 6th paragraph (ChapterContentView.swift anchorStride) and ChapterTracking.topmostAnchor picks the paragraph near the viewport TOP, so a fully-read 60-paragraph one-shot tops out around 48/59 ≈ 0.81 — below both isFinished thresholds (≥0.99, or ≥0.95 for complete works; ReadingStatSnapshot.isFinished in Fanficly/Reader/ReadingProgressStore.swift:90-92). Works read to the last line show "81% read" forever, never earn the Finished badge, and never count in Stats "stories read". Fix: detect end-of-content explicitly — always report an anchor for the final paragraph regardless of stride and treat bottom-of-content-visible as progress 1.0 (or compute progress from scroll offset). Mind that maxProgress only ever advances (by design) and page-by-page mode has a milder version (anchor = first paragraph of current page, ReaderView.swift:1132-1138).

Add tests where feasible (ChapterTrackingTests covers anchor math; ReadingStatsAggregator is pure). input.title: Stop stale widget taps regressing reading position
input.prompt:
Fix a confirmed reading-position regression in Fanficly's widget resume flow (repo /Users/jenny/Work/ao3-app), found by an adversarially-verified multi-agent audit:

RootView.installResumeProgressIfAvailable (Fanficly/RootView.swift:277-304) prefers the anchor baked into the tapped widget's deep-link URL (route.anchor ?? widgetAnchor, ~line 292). Two failure paths: (1) ReadingProgressStore.save stamps ReadingProgress.updatedAt and the widget payload with the same `now` (ReadingProgressStore.swift:15-54), so the strict-greater freshness guard `existing.updatedAt > matchingWidgetProgress.freshnessDate` (RootView.swift:281-284) never trips for the current work — and WidgetKit timeline reloads are budget-throttled, so the home-screen widget URL can lag hours behind. (2) If the user has since read a DIFFERENT work, WidgetProgressStore.load() returns that other work, matchingWidgetProgress is nil, and the freshness guard is skipped entirely. Scenario: read work A to chapter 10; the widget still shows chapter 2 from this morning; tapping it rewrites ReadingProgress to chapter 2 and the chapter-10 position is lost (save overwrites unconditionally).

Fix: never let a URL anchor move progress backwards — only apply route.anchor/widget anchor when it is strictly fresher than the existing ReadingProgress for that work (compare with >=, prefer the widget-store anchor over the URL anchor when the store entry is newer); otherwise just navigate and let the locally saved progress win. Note CLAUDE.md's warning: openResumeRoute must NOT clear detailPath itself — keep the atomic pendingResumeRoute/.task(id:) push pattern intact.

Test what's testable (RootView.parseResumeRoute parsing exists; the freshness comparison can be extracted into a pure helper and unit-tested). Run: DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer xcodebuild test -project Fanficly.xcodeproj -scheme Fanficly -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO -only-testing:FanficlyTests
input.tldr: Tapping an out-of-date home-screen widget can silently rewind your saved reading position — make the resume route only ever move progress forward.

input.title: Make reader-profile deletion survive iCloud KVS merge
input.prompt:
Fix a confirmed bug where deleted reader profiles resurrect in Fanficly (repo /Users/jenny/Work/ao3-app), found by an adversarially-verified multi-agent audit:

ReaderView.deleteProfile (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderView.swift:128-141) and ReaderSettingsView.deleteProfile remove the profile and call saveProfiles → ReaderProfileSyncStore.publishLocalProfiles (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderProfileSyncStore.swift:25-38). publishLocalProfiles merges the new local list INTO the cloud copy via ReaderProfile.mergedProfiles (Fanficly/Reader/ReaderProfile.swift:141-153), which is a pure union starting from the cloud list — it never removes anything — and writes the merged JSON (deleted profile included) straight back to UserDefaults "reader.profiles". So a deleted profile reappears immediately (NSUbiquitousKeyValueStore caches locally, so this happens even without an active iCloud account), or at latest on the next didChangeExternallyNotification via syncCloudToLocal (lines 40-59). Deletion never sticks on any device once the profile was ever published.

Fix properly with deletions as first-class: add a per-profile updatedAt or a tombstone list (deleted names + timestamps) to the synced JSON, and have mergedProfiles drop profiles whose tombstone is newer than their entry. Keep backward compatibility with existing synced JSON that lacks the new fields (older app versions must still decode — the ReaderProfile struct is Codable with optional-field tolerance; follow the widthRaw precedent). Minimal stopgap if the full design is too invasive: publish the local list as-is in publishLocalProfiles (local is authoritative for deletions) and only union in syncCloudToLocal.

ReaderProfile merge logic is pure and already covered in FanficlyTests (PersistenceTests exercise ReaderProfile merging) — add cases for delete-then-merge and tombstone expiry. Run: DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer xcodebuild test -project Fanficly.xcodeproj -scheme Fanficly -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO -only-testing:FanficlyTests
input.tldr: Deleting a reader typography profile doesn't stick — the iCloud key-value merge unions it right back. Add tombstones so deletions propagate.

name: audit-2026-07-advisory-backlog
description: Minor confirmed-by-audit Fanficly issues not yet fixed or chipped (July 2026 multi-agent audit)
metadata:
  type: project
---

A 61-agent adversarially-verified audit (2026-07-09) confirmed 18 serious findings. The serious ones were fixed in-session or spawned as task chips (iCloud LWW backup, subscriptions reliability, stats accuracy, Popular facets markup, widget stale-tap, profile tombstones). These **advisory/minor** items remain unaddressed and are worth picking up opportunistically:

- `ao3PathEncode` encodes apostrophe as `*at*` — AO3 404s on fandoms with apostrophes (AO3Endpoints.swift).
- Logout can leave the live AO3 session cookie in the Keychain despite UI saying it's cleared (Auth/Credentials.swift).
- TTS auto-advance stalls with stale state on a chapter with no speakable text (SpeechController.swift).
- Folder deep link uses the clear-then-push navigation pattern the widget resume route was explicitly fixed to avoid (RootView.swift).
- False "new work" notifications for followed authors when an old work is updated (AuthorWorksView.swift).
- Stats backfill gives finished single-chapter works maxProgress 0, so old one-shots never count as read (ReadingProgressStore.swift).
- "not rated" search alias unreachable — the exclusion extractor consumes it first (SearchPromptParser.swift).
- Reading span bucketed entirely into the day it *ends* (overnight reads credit the wrong day).
- AsyncImage re-downloads story images on page turns (URLCache.shared unreliable for large images); consider a small memory cache if images feel slow.
- Toggling "Show images in stories" shifts paragraph indices, so saved positions drift by the number of images above the anchor (accepted trade-off, documented in ReaderView comment near the `reader.showImages` @AppStorage).

Related: [[android-port-parity]] — none of this is ported to Android either.

content.text: Everything is complete. Final summary: --- ## What happened **PR #21 (freeform tag fix) — errors fixed, CI green.** The failure was a stale test, not the fix itself: `test_bestMatch_fallsBackToFirst` asserted that a freeform lookup falls back to AO3's top autocomplete suggestion — exactly the behavior the PR intentionally removes. I retargeted the test at a character lookup (where top-suggestion fallback is still correct and powers ship-via-character resolution), updated `bestMatch`'s doc comment, and pushed. [Build & Test now passes](https://github.com/yennster/fanficly/actions/runs/29041066317/job/86198064151). **PR #20 (throttle fix) — validated: good fix, with one confirmed defect, now also fixed and green.** A 9-agent validation workflow (4 review lenses + adversarial verification) confirmed the root-cause analysis empirically: the old `ThrottleActor` really did let concurrent callers burst (the repo-wide bug hunt independently rediscovered the same bug). The actor fix and its regression test are correct — merge-worthy on sight. But the new 429 retry was a **politeness regression**: it ignored `Retry-After` and re-hit AO3 with 0.5–1s backoff when a real clamp-down is always longer, tripling load on exactly the screens the PR was fixing. I pushed a follow-up commit that only retries within a short (≤10s) `Retry-After` and otherwise fails fast like main did, and dropped `.notConnectedToInternet` from the retryable set. CI is green. Known non-blocking follow-up: the retry half has no test coverage (needs a URLProtocol stub). **Image toggle — implemented, default off (uncommitted in the working tree).** Settings → Reader now has a "Show images in stories" toggle (`reader.showImages`, global — it's a content/privacy choice, not typography, so it's deliberately not part of reader profiles). When on, `` tags become fixed-height inline image slots in all three reading modes, loaded via AsyncImage from the author's image host. Off is byte-identical to today's text-only behavior. Key design points: image slots occupy real paragraph indices so reading anchors, TTS karaoke, and progress stay aligned (TTS skips them silently); slots are fixed-height in every mode so a late-loading image can never shove your restored position off-screen; `data:`/`javascript:`/root-relative srcs are rejected, http upgrades to https, and images are never allowed to point at archiveofourown.org itself (image loads bypass the throttle and carry the session cookie). The settings copy is honest about IP exposure and iOS's temporary cache. **Audit — 61 agents, 39 findings, 18 adversarially confirmed.** Beyond the image-toggle polish above, I fixed the two contained pre-existing bugs directly: - **Crash**: `SearchPromptParser` threw `NSRangeException` on prompts with Turkish `İ` (lowercasing changes UTF-16 length, desyncing its parallel buffers) — now uses a length-preserving fold. - **Cache poisoning**: `TagResolver` permanently cached failed resolutions, so one offline search broke that tag's canonicalization until relaunch — failures are no longer memoized. All **202 unit tests pass** (13 new ones cover images, the crash, and the cache fix). The six big confirmed findings are queued as task chips you can launch individually — the worst is a genuine **data-loss blocker**: iCloud backup is whole-file last-writer-wins, so a second device with a smaller library silently shrinks the backup (chips: iCloud data loss, subscription reliability, stats accuracy, Popular-tab facets that never matched live AO3 markup, stale-widget position regression, profile-deletion resurrection). Minor advisory items are saved to memory so they aren't lost. **One caveat**: the working tree touches `TagResolver.swift`/`TagResolverTests.swift`, which PR #21 also modifies (different hunks). Commit the local changes before merging PR #21, or tell me and I'll split them into a PR for you.

extracted title/creator text from the original-case buffer using the
same NSRanges. Characters like Turkish "I-dot" (U+0130) lowercase to
two UTF-16 units, desyncing the buffers: substring(with:) then threw
an uncaught NSRangeException ("Istanbul by:melis" crashed the app),
or silently extracted shifted text when the range stayed in bounds.

Lowercase character-by-character, keeping any character whose
lowercase form would change its UTF-16 width - those simply don't
match the lowercase-only patterns, like any other non-ASCII letter.

Found by adversarially-verified multi-agent audit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
